correctness.rationale: The successful-deposition state process on C_L is finite and absorbing: a terminal empty site must have two opposite occupied neighbors. First accepted deposition leaves an interval of L−1 vacancies bounded by the same species. For auxiliary m-site intervals, first successful transitions at two ends occur at rate 1/2 and interior attempts rate 1, giving (m−1)a_m=a_(m−1)+sum_{j=1}^{m−2}(a_j+b_j) and analogous b. Subtracting proves b_m−a_m=1/(m−1)!, and the generating function ODE yields A(z)=[e^(−z)/(1−z)^2−e^z]/2, B=A+e^z. Coefficient extraction gives exact E X_L for all L≥3; difference of consecutive blocked-site fractions is strictly positive. Coupled first-arrival local-minimum shields bound the origin's dependence on distant sites and identify the infinite-line limit. Independent Fraction calculations matched n=3..11 including E X4=1/2, E X5=5/6, E X6=13/12; finite tests do not establish the all-L recurrence.
